checklist.detail: Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy: computed wall temp 1657 K EXCEEDS its 1250 K max service temp (Tc 3700 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~11.9 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3642 K, coolant ~35 m/s (coolant-side wall ~871 K), 0.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.
checklist.name: Chamber material thermal margin

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the nozzle (area ratio ~6.2, radiative): wall ~2207 K, 0.57x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~6.0), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~17.4 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.4 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~6.4 mm channel width, this reversed ~17.0 MPa differential is ~390 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
